sentences.text: 1 With the consent of the parties, heard finally at motion stage.

2.This appeal has been filed by the appellant under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the award dated 19.1.2023 passed in MACC No.500137/2015 by 4th Addl. Member, MACT,
Rewa seeking setting aside of impugned award and for grant of suitable compensation.
3.

Learned counsel for the appellant, after referring to deposition of applicant witness Dr. Uday Singh as well as permanent disability certificate Ex.P/8, submits that Tribunal has wrongly discarded above medical evidence and has held that appellant failed to prove its case regarding disability on account of injuries sustained in the accident.
It is also urged that Tribunal has not awarded any amount for future treatment/ removal of implants.
It is also urged that Tribunal has not awarded appropriate amount for nourishing diet, conveyance charges etc.

Therefore,
compensation awarded by the Tribunal be suitably enhanced.
4. Learned counsel for the respondent no. 3 submits that findings recorded by the Tribunal are just and proper.
No interferenfce is required in the same.
Hence, the appeal filed by the appellant be dismissed.
5. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.
6. So far as permanent disability is concerned, in the instant case, accident occurred on 17.12.2014 and certificate Ex.P/8 has been issued on 11.5.2017.

Further, from testimony of Doctor Uday Singh,
it is clear that before issuing above certificate, no scientific tests have been conducted and just only on the basis of clinical examination, Ex.P/8 has been prepared\issued.
Further applicant witness Suresh has not specifically mentioned in his testimony nature of permanent disability suffered by him on account of injuries sustained in the accident.
Learned Tribunal in para 12, after relying upon the judgment Rajkumar Vs. Ajay Kumar, AIR Online 2010 SC 125, has held that no scientific test has been conducted.

entities.text: Rajkumar Vs. Ajay Kumar, AIR Online 2010 SC 125
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, disability certificate cannot be relied upon and on the basis of such certificate, it cannot be held that appellant has suffered permanent disability.

7. In view of discussion in the forgoing paras, in this Court's considered opinion, it cannot be said that findings recorded by the Tribunal in para 12 are perverse and are against evidence on record.
8. So far as amount of compensation is concerned, summary discharge ticket Ex.P/10 reveals that implants have been removed on 22.2.2018.
Further, appellant has not examined any doctor and has not filed any medical documents to show that appellant needs further/future treatment.

Therefore,
no amount can be awarded under the above head.
9. Tribunal has awarded Rs.35,000/- for pain and suffering.

Rs.15000/- for nourishing diet,
Rs.10,000-/ for conveyance charges, apart from medical expenses.
It is evident from Ex.P/8, P/9 and P/10 that the appellant remained hospitalized from 19.12.2014 to 01.01.2015 and from 21.2.2018 to 24.2.2018.
In view of above period of hospitalization, no enhancement is required in above heads.

sentences.text: So far as loss of income during treatment is concerned, on the date of accident, minimum wages of an unskilled labour were Rs.5895/- per month.
Therefore, appellant is entitled to receive

Rs.
17,685/- loss of income during treatment period
. Compensation awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced by Rs.2685/-.
11. Hence, appeal filed by the appellant is partly allowed.
enhanced Compensation of Rs.2685/- shall carry interest at the rate determined by the Tribunal.
Other findings of the Tribunal shall remain intact.
12. Appeal filed by the appellant is disposed off accordingly.

(ACHAL KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE Hashmi (
